newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CEZ '96 power supply prices set up 0.2pct.
newsitem.headline: CEZ '96 power supply prices set up 0.2pct.

text.p: The Czech Finance Ministry on Thursday said that it had set the prices the main power supplier CEZ a.s. can charge regional distributors for 1996 supplies, including retroactive billing, an average of 0.2 percent higher than in 1995.

The ruling comes after a long-debated agreement between CEZ and eight regional distributors over revenue sharing from power sales. The price equates to 1,035 crowns per megawatt hour, versus 1,033 crowns in 1995.

The agreement, which Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy announced on Monday without revealing the price agreed, was hammered out between representatives of CEZ, the distributors and government officials.
Dlouhy said the deal may be "hard to accept for some of the distributors" but declined to elaborate.
